title: n8n Overview
description: Monitor n8n workflow automation performance, queue health, runtime saturation, and security activity. Groups are ordered top to bottom by troubleshooting priority: start at Overview, then drill into the specific subsystem the failing alert points at.

definition.content:
# n8n Workflow Automation

Get end-to-end visibility into your n8n deployment:
- Workflow execution and queue health
- Per-node performance
- Cache and Node.js runtime usage
- Audit and SSO activity for security

# Useful Links

[GitHub Repo](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n)

[n8n official documentation](https://docs.n8n.io/)

[n8n home page](https://n8n.io/)

Pick a workflow from the **Workflow** selector at the top to scope this whole view.

Read top to bottom: KPIs and monitors flag whether anything's wrong, the lifecycle and duration charts show when it changed, the per-host failure rate table tells you which host is affected, and the event timeline + error logs reveal what happened.

If the per-workflow metric widgets are empty, your n8n needs `N8N_METRICS_INCLUDE_WORKFLOW_ID_LABEL=true` — workflow-scoped metrics are opt-in.

Track how your workflows are running over time. Watch throughput, success rate, and execution duration. A duration spike with a stable success rate often points to a slow downstream node (check the Node Execution group); a success rate drop with stable duration usually points to a single failing workflow.

Track overall node execution across your workflows. A start rate that consistently exceeds the finish rate means nodes are being invoked but not completing — commonly an external service timing out (such as an HTTP node). For a per-node breakdown, see the `Top nodes with failed executions` toplist in the Overview group, which uses log data. In queue mode, this requires `QUEUE_HEALTH_CHECK_ACTIVE=true` on your workers.

Monitor your queue-mode deployment. Track the job backlog, processing rate, and stalled jobs. A rising backlog with a falling dequeue rate suggests your workers are slow or down; a climbing stalled count suggests workers are crashing mid-job. Queue mode only.

Track how each n8n worker is picking up and completing tasks. A worker that goes idle while the queue backlog is rising is usually the one to investigate first — often a stuck task runner or a lost Redis connection. Requires `QUEUE_HEALTH_CHECK_ACTIVE=true` on your workers.

definition.title: Request → response gap (>0 = worker dropping tasks)

definition.content: Monitor cache hit rate and operations. A hit rate dropping below ~80% often indicates a recently changed workflow that hasn't warmed its cache yet. A sudden spike in cache updates without matching reads can mean a workflow is writing far more entries than it uses.

Track inbound webhook and API traffic — request rate, latency, and response codes. A latency climb localized to a single status code (especially 4xx or 5xx) usually points to one endpoint or caller; the request rate chart helps confirm whether the affected traffic share is significant.

Track the health of the underlying Node.js runtime — event-loop lag, heap usage, and garbage collection. Sustained event-loop lag or heap usage at the ceiling usually means GC pressure is bleeding into workflow latency. Cross-check with workflow execution duration to confirm the runtime is the cause.

definition.title: Event loop lag min / max / stddev

definition.content: Monitor instance-level resource usage and health across your n8n deployment — CPU, memory, uptime, and readiness checks. Watch `Last Activity` for stalled workers, and confirm `Readiness Check` is green before declaring an instance healthy.

Track AI node activity in your workflows (n8n 2.x) — LLM generations, errors, and vector store usage. A rising LLM error rate with a flat generation rate often indicates a provider-side issue (rate limit, expired key, outage). Vector store ingestion without matching searches often signals an unfinished workflow.

An overview of total workflows, credentials, users, and executions in your deployment. Sudden drops in workflows or credentials are often the first signal of an accidental bulk delete — cross-check with the Audit Activity group. Available on n8n 2.x when `N8N_METRICS_INCLUDE_WORKFLOW_STATISTICS=true` is set.

Track the performance of n8n's expression engine — evaluation latency and worker pool health. A workflow slowdown that doesn't show up in the Node Execution group often appears here (slow `{{ ... }}` expressions). Pool replenish failures suggest the V8 isolate pool is exhausted — consider raising `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_POOL_*`. Available when `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm` and `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true` are set.

Monitor security-related events such as logins, workflow changes, and credential access. A burst of failed logins followed by a successful one from a new IP can indicate credential stuffing. A burst of workflow deletions without a matching deploy can indicate an accidental bulk delete. Repeated execution-data reveal failures usually point to a permission misconfiguration.

Track embed and SSO token exchange activity for embedded n8n deployments. A failure rate climb here without a matching workflow failure rate climb usually points to an authentication issue rather than a workflow issue.
Stream n8n application logs filtered by severity. Use error and warning logs to investigate workflow failures and correlate them with the metric anomalies shown above.

query.query_string: source:n8n host:$host.value status:(error OR critical) (@n8n.workflow_id_lower:$workflow.value OR -@n8n.workflow_id_lower:*)
